components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default dark button — inverts to Signal Lime on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #0F1412; color: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid rgba(15,20,18,0.2); border-radius: 20px; padding: 14px 28px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 16px; box-shadow: 0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); transition: all 0.3s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #CDFB47; color: #0F1412; border-color: #CDFB47; transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #CDFB47, 0 0 0 4px rgba(205,251,71,0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); }

components.name: Lime CTA Button
components.description: The primary call-to-action voice — Signal Lime fill, inverts to Circuit Black on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-lime">Start Your Project <svg width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="12" x2="19" y2="12"/><polyline points="12 5 19 12 12 19"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-lime { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: #CDFB47; color: #0F1412; border: none; border-radius: 20px; padding: 16px 32px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; box-shadow: 0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); transition: all 0.3s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-lime:hover { background: #0F1412; color: #FFFFFF; transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-lime:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #CDFB47, 0 0 0 4px rgba(205,251,71,0.3); } .ds-btn-lime:active { transform: scale(0.97); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Default glassmorphic card — soft shadow at rest, lift + hover shadow on interaction.

Complete digital solutions in 5 days — website, admin panel, Android & iOS apps.
components.css: .ds-card { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.80); backdrop-filter: blur(20px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(20px); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.60); border-radius: 32px; padding: 32px; box-shadow: 0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); transition: all 0.3s ease; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-8px); box-shadow: 0 35px 80px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); border-color: rgba(205,251,71,0.5); } .ds-card-title { font-family: Fraunces, serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 20px; color: #0F1412; margin: 0 0 12px; } .ds-card-body { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; color: #737373; margin: 0; }

components.css: .ds-status-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 12px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; border: 1px solid transparent; } .ds-status-active { background: rgba(16,185,129,0.10); color: #059669; border-color: rgba(16,185,129,0.30); } .ds-status-inactive { background: #F3F4F6; color: #6B7280; border-color: #E5E7EB; }

components.name: Lightfall Signature Backdrop
components.description: Static CSS approximation of the hero's live WebGL shader (OGL-based Lightfall) — lime/dark light-streak trails. The real implementation renders on canvas via WebGL; this snippet is a representative, self-contained stand-in for the panel.
components.css: .ds-lightfall { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 240px; background: #0F1412; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 40px; } .ds-lightfall-streak { position: absolute; top: -20%; width: 2px; height: 140%; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(205,251,71,0) 0%, #CDFB47 50%, rgba(169,229,31,0) 100%); opacity: 0.7; filter: blur(0.5px); } .ds-lightfall-streak-1 { left: 20%; animation: ds-lightfall-fall 3s linear infinite; } .ds-lightfall-streak-2 { left: 55%; animation: ds-lightfall-fall 4s linear infinite 0.8s; } .ds-lightfall-streak-3 { left: 80%; animation: ds-lightfall-fall 3.5s linear infinite 1.6s; } @keyframes ds-lightfall-fall { from { transform: translateY(-20%); } to { transform: translateY(20%); } }

narrative.overview:
This project has two coherent, deliberately different visual systems. The marketing site (Persuade mode: home, about, services, projects, blog, contact) reads as a dark, focused engineering console rather than a conventional marketing site. Deep near-black (#0F1412) is the resting state of every major surface — nav, hero, CTA banners — and Signal Lime (#CDFB47) exists to mean exactly one thing wherever it appears: this is active, this is happening now. It's the terminal cursor, the build-success indicator, the status light — never decoration for its own sake. The hero's live WebGL shader backdrop and the code-preview card ("Live Build Succeeded (14ms)") aren't incidental flourishes; they're the thesis made literal.

Against that dark, technical foundation sits a warm counterweight: Fraunces, a high-contrast display serif, carries every headline. The pairing — engineering-console color language with editorial serif type — is the system's core tension and its signature.

The admin/CRM dashboard and client portal (Operate mode: /dashboard, /portal) share the same two core tokens but apply them functionally, not atmospherically: a light gray canvas (#F5F6F4), white panels, tight 8-16px radii, and Signal Lime used as a solid active-state fill (sidebar, not a rare accent mark). Motion is fast and restrained (FadeIn, not scroll-triggered Reveal/Stagger). This is a deliberate split, not an unfinished corner of the marketing system — assume Persuade mode below unless a section is marked Operate.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black is the default surface; white is the content canvas; lime is a rare, meaningful signal — never a background wash (Persuade mode).
Fraunces serif for all display/headline type; Inter for body and UI; JetBrains Mono only for actual code/data.
Soft, large-blur ambient shadows and glassmorphism (never hard-offset or neobrutalist) in Persuade mode.
Generous pill/rounded-full shapes for interactive chrome against softer large-radius rounding (32-40px) for content surfaces in Persuade mode.
Operate mode (dashboard/portal) trades all of the above for a calmer, denser, functional system: light gray canvas, white panels, tight 8-16px radii, fast non-scroll-hijacking motion.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime never appears as a passive background fill or large color block — only as a small, meaningful mark (text, icon, thin accent line, active-state fill) that says "this is live." A full-bleed lime panel would break the rule.

rules.name: The Two-Surface Rule
rules.body: Every section is either Circuit Black or Paper White at rest — no mid-tone gray section backgrounds. Contrast between sections is the rhythm.

rules.name: The Serif-Only-Display Rule
rules.body: Fraunces never appears below Title size, and Inter never carries a headline. The split is absolute — it's what makes the pairing read as a deliberate choice rather than inconsistency.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Hover Rule
rules.body: Interactive cards are flat-ish at rest and gain both a translateY lift and a shadow escalation on hover — depth is a response to interaction, not a static decoration.

dos: Do treat Signal Lime as a rare mark of "this is active" — CTA fills, active states, live indicators — never a large background field (The Signal Rule).
Do keep every section's resting background either Circuit Black or Paper White — no mid-tone gray sections.
Do pair large soft-blur shadows with a hover lift on any interactive card or button; nothing gets a hard-offset shadow.

Do give every clickable card/row a real keyboard path (role, tabIndex, visible focus ring) — this system has a Card primitive that does this automatically when onClick is passed; use it rather than a bare onClick div.
Do hide duplicate/looping marquee content from assistive tech (aria-hidden on the repeated copy) — this system runs several infinite-scroll marquees.
donts: Don't introduce a second "accent" hex outside #CDFB47 (Signal Lime). One isolated instance of #65A30D currently exists in the "Why Choose Us" eyebrow badge — treat it as a bug to consolidate to the primary token, not a precedent for a secondary accent.
Don't use text-gray-400/text-slate-400 (or lighter) for body text on a white surface — both fall below the 4.5:1 AA contrast floor. gray-500/slate-500 is the lightest acceptable gray on white.

Don't run a continuous JS-driven animation (marquees, shaders) without gating it behind IntersectionObserver — several components in this system pause off-screen for exactly this reason; new ones should too.
Don't use Fraunces below Title size, or Inter for a headline — the serif/sans split is absolute, not a suggestion.
